issues.claim: gap_for_local_installer: "Every credible shelf-intelligence vendor is built for chains: robots that need wide aisles and 5,000+ sq ft"
issues.problem: Overstates Simbe's published requirement. The cited FAQ says a store should be bigger than a convenience store, i.e. >1,000 sq ft, and only that most of its stores are >5,000 sq ft. Presented as a hard 5,000+ sq ft need, which the source does not say. (The same brief states the FAQ correctly elsewhere, so it is an internal inconsistency, not a fabrication.)
issues.fix: Rewrite as "most Tally deployments are >5,000 sq ft, with a stated minimum of >1,000 sq ft" or drop the square-footage qualifier from this sentence.

issues.claim: existing_solutions > Zippedi: 8-hour scanning shift, overhead camera up to 7 m, high-res tag cameras, depth sensors, optional RFID, "specs as published on the vendor's Zippy page", source_url = robot-distribution.com
issues.problem: The specs are real but not on the cited URL. The Robot Distribution page only covers acquisition modes and EU compliance; it does not list the 8-hour shift, 7 m overhead camera or RFID specs. The specs appear on zippedi.com/zippy, which is not cited. Sourcing mismatch, values themselves are correct.
issues.fix: Set source_url to https://www.zippedi.com/zippy for the spec sentence and keep the distributor URL for the pricing/acquisition sentence.

issues.claim: existing_solutions > Pensa: "Captures shelf images with handheld or drone devices and reports gaps and shelf conditions"
issues.problem: The cited Pensa case study says store associates scanned and that the whole store took ~35 minutes, but does not mention handheld or drone capture. Unsupported by the cited page (it is a product-page claim, not a number).
issues.fix: Cite a Pensa product page for handheld/drone capture, or drop the device detail and keep only the case-study findings.

issues.claim: legal_privacy > "N.J.A.C. 13:47C-3.5 ... a subchapter that contains the building-materials advertising rule at 13:47C-3.4 and covers nonfoodstuffs packaging and quantity rules"
issues.problem: Imprecise. The rule text expressly carves 13:47C-3.4 (advertising of building materials) OUT of the $100 penalty in (a) and gives it its own $50-$500 schedule in (b). The brief's wording implies 3.4 sits inside the $100-per-package penalty. The conclusion (this is not the retail price-marking penalty) is still correct.
issues.fix: Add the carve-out: "$100 minimum per violation, each package separate, for this subchapter except 13:47C-3.4, which has its own $50-$500 schedule."

issues.claim: legal_privacy > pricing/tag obligation: "Separately, the Unit Pricing Disclosure Act requires standard unit pricing for regulated grocery commodities (New Jersey is one of nine states with such a law)." source_url = njconsumeraffairs.gov CFA PDF
issues.problem: The Consumer Fraud Act compilation does not contain the Unit Pricing Disclosure Act or the nine-state claim; that sentence is unsupported at the cited URL. It is supported by the cited NJ OAG Walmart release, which is used elsewhere in the brief.
issues.fix: Add the OAG Walmart release as a second source for that sentence, or move the sentence to the enforcement-risk bullet that already cites it.

issues.claim: fit_score: legal_risk_low = 10, while the rationale says "Legal risk is moderate-low, not low"
issues.problem: Labelling inconsistency (arithmetic is fine: 13+10+8+13+10+6 = 60). The rationale's own text argues against calling the risk low while the sub-score is a high-ish 10, which reads as a contradiction to a reader comparing the two.
issues.fix: Either reword the rationale ("comparatively low: video-only, no audio, no biometrics, NJDPA thresholds far out of reach; residual items are unconfirmed, not adverse") or drop the sub-score to reflect "moderate".

issues.claim: models_and_tools > Cactus: "Fine-tuning tooling is documented for its text and speech models, not its vision model."
issues.problem: Not visible on the cited model card, which documents the runtime, targets and three model families but no fine-tuning tooling for any of them. Cannot be confirmed from the cited page.
issues.fix: Cite the specific docs page that covers Needle/Whistle fine-tuning, or soften to "fine-tuning support for the vision model is not documented on the model card."
